BogSignal / Argos · 15 November 2026

Wetland segmentation:
NISAR interferometry experiments

Report for the completed seed-0, five-fold InSAR experiments

Executive findings

Interferometric coherence added useful weak-reference signal for swamp. Adding the InSAR layers to the 14-channel U-Net raised swamp/marsh average precision from 48.2% to 50.7% (+2.5 points; higher in 4 of 5 folds) and swamp average precision from 31.3% to 37.2% (higher in 4 of 5 folds). Marsh and permanent water did not improve.

Coherence alone did at least as well as all 27 InSAR layers. Nine coherence layers gave 53.2% swamp/marsh average precision against 50.7% for the 27-layer variant; phase homogeneity and phase offset added little beyond it.

Training Swamp and Marsh as one class did not improve the ranking. Swamp/marsh average precision was 47.9% against 48.2% for the baseline (higher in 3 of 5 folds). It raised the IoU of the most-likely-class map from 24.9% to 29.7% (higher in 5 of 5 folds), mainly by drawing more wetland. Its Marsh score is not meaningful, because Marsh is no longer a separate training class.

The fringe method of Hübinger et al. (2026) did not produce a wetland map from 12-day summer pairs. It flagged 71% of the radar frame as water under vegetation at every inferred date. Reference Swamp was flagged as often as Other (85% against 82%); only Permanent water differed (23%). The method needs a water-level change of a full fringe, about 12 cm along the line of sight; the median local phase change over coherent Swamp was 0.12 rad, about 0.2 cm.

The most-likely-class map under-draws every class except Other. It assigns 88.5% of scored pixels to Other against 78.1% in the reference. Cross-fitted per-class offsets restore the class areas and raise baseline swamp/marsh recall from 33.6% to 47.5%, with reference precision falling from 61.1% to 48.5%.

Recommendation: keep coherence as the candidate InSAR input for the next model version, in its nine-layer form. Do not use the fringe method on 12-day pairs; retest it only on pairs at least 36 days apart or across the spring flood. Confirm the swamp gain with more seeds and on further radar frames before changing the published model D.

These are five-fold validation results against historical/inferred weak labels, not independent contemporary wetland accuracy. Every variant uses one training seed and the 1,061 train and validation patches inside one radar frame. The test set remains unscored.

1. Study question and fixed design

The earlier A–D experiments used NISAR backscatter. This study adds NISAR interferograms, which record for two passes how the radar phase changed and how alike the passes are (coherence). The objective was to assess whether measures derived from interferograms improve the six-class U-Net beyond its 14 input channels, and whether the unsupervised fringe workflow of Hübinger, Fluet-Chouinard, Escobar and Jaramillo (Remote Sensing of Environment 332, 115086) maps water under vegetation in Polissia.

How to read the metrics

For combined wetland results, the Swamp and Marsh probabilities are summed first. The main tables rank pixels by that probability; the hard class maps are treated separately in section 4.

  • Average precision: quality of the ranking of pixels by swamp/marsh probability. With 3.1% reference prevalence, a random ranking scores about that value.
  • Recall at 5% area: fraction of reference swamp/marsh pixels recovered by inspecting the highest-scoring 5% of the scored area.
  • IoU: overlap of a hard class map with the reference. Recall and reference precision in section 4 describe the same maps.
  • AUC (feature test only): ranking quality where 50% is chance.
  • Higher in k of 5 folds: number of folds in which a variant beat the baseline. Folds differ far more from each other than variants do within a fold.

2. Do the InSAR measures separate the reference classes?

Before any training, 400,000 labelled pixels were sampled from the frame and each class was ranked from InSAR measures alone, using gradient-boosted trees with four-fold cross-validation over 20 km blocks. The thresholded detector is close to chance for every class (swamp/marsh AUC 0.60). Season summaries recover part of the signal and keeping each pair separate recovers most of it (0.88). Coherence by itself carries the larger part (0.80). This motivated passing per-pair layers to the U-Net instead of a thresholded map.

4. Decision rule: most likely class versus fitted offsets

Choosing the single most likely class per pixel under-draws every class except Other, because Other is far more common and is chosen whenever the model is unsure. The training code's tune_bias adds one offset per class to the log-probabilities before the choice. Here the offsets are cross-fitted: those applied to a fold's patches were fitted on the held-out predictions of the other four folds, so no patch helped choose its own rule.

The fitted offsets bring each class area close to the reference. They recover more reference swamp/marsh and confirm a smaller share of what they map; the choice depends on whether missing wetland or mapping too much is the costlier error. Peatland stays the weakest class under both rules.

6. The fringe method of Hübinger et al. on 12-day pairs

The published workflow (sections 2.2–2.3 of the paper) was implemented as --method paper: Canny edge detection on the Gaussian-smoothed wrapped phase finds fringe turnovers; fringe lines are buffered by three pixels; homogeneous-phase regions come from a local variance filter with a morphological clean-up; only connected homogeneous regions that touch a fringe are kept. This is repeated 100 times per interferogram with random parameters. Pixels flagged in at least 80% of runs form the pair's mask, consecutive pairs are joined to give the extent at each date, and pixels are sorted into flagged at every date, at some dates, or never. The method uses no labels.

Two choices are ours because the paper's main text leaves them open: the parameter ranges (the paper's are in its supplementary Table S2) and a circular form of the local variance, so that the −π/π wrap itself does not count as noise. Canny thresholds are set as a share of the response of a full turnover.

“Never flagged” is not “dry”: open water returns no stable phase, so the method cannot flag it. Reference labels and model D in this figure are the website's regional layers at about 340 m, warped to the radar grid.

Over the 8 inferred dates, 43,803 of 61,333 km² were flagged at every date. Where model D predicts swamp/marsh, the method flags every date for 83% of pixels; where model D predicts Other, for 72%. Removing the regional phase over a 5 km window before fringe detection (9 of 9 interferograms processed) left no land flagged in at least 80 of 100 runs, while 83% to 98% was flagged in at least one run: single runs still mark almost everything or nothing, and no stable local detections remain.

Why the method has nothing to detect here

Reference classMedian local phase change90th percentilePixels above a quarter fringe
Other0.10 rad / 0.2 cm0.27 rad / 0.5 cm0.29%
Swamp0.12 rad / 0.2 cm0.39 rad / 0.7 cm1.53%
Marsh0.12 rad / 0.2 cm0.37 rad / 0.7 cm0.77%
Permanent water0.19 rad / 0.4 cm1.14 rad / 2.2 cm6.49%
Peatland cropland0.12 rad / 0.2 cm0.35 rad / 0.7 cm0.56%
Peatland non-cropland0.10 rad / 0.2 cm0.28 rad / 0.5 cm0.42%

Local phase change is the absolute offset from a 5 km background on pixels with coherence above 0.4; one radian is 1.9 cm along the line of sight. Without local fringes, the only turnovers are broad atmospheric and orbital ramps. Over 12 days nearly all land stays coherent and forms one connected homogeneous region, so a single such turnover marks all of it. The paper used pairs 46 to 219 days apart over a tropical floodplain, where non-flooded forest loses coherence and water levels move by much more.

7. What the same interferograms do carry: coherence

Coherence needs no water-level change. Across the nine pairs, Swamp + Marsh was the steadiest reference class (mean 0.52), Peatland cropland changed most among land classes (0.42) and Permanent water stayed near the noise level (0.36).

This is the signal the InSAR layers pass to the U-Net. Low coherence over farmed peat is consistent with mowing, harvest and ploughing between passes, but coherence also falls with rain and with longer gaps, so it is evidence of surface change, not of its cause.

8. Interpretation, limitations and stopping point

  • Weak references: labels are historical/inferred and can be incomplete, wrong or temporally mismatched. Other is not verified dry land. Peatland classes outside Poland derive from a product with about 1 km detail.
  • One seed, one frame: no repeated-seed uncertainty was estimated, and the patch pool lies inside a single radar frame. The direction of the swamp gain is supported by most folds; its size is not established.
  • Fold spread: the same recipe ranges widely across folds. Differences of a few points between variants should remain inconclusive.
  • Decision offsets: cross-fitting keeps each patch out of its own rule, but the offsets are fitted and scored against the same weak labels.
  • Fringe method scope: it was applied with our own parameter ranges to NASA's standard 12-day product. The result says nothing about longer pairs, spring flood dates or the paper's own setting.
  • Provisional products: the interferograms are provisional NISAR releases and may be reprocessed.
  • Stopping point: conclude this phase with coherence as a candidate input. Repeating with three seeds, extending to track 172 (catalogued, not downloaded) and building pairs of 36 days or more from single-pass scenes belong to follow-up work.

9. Reproducibility and retained artifacts

All fold checkpoints are retained under runs/exp/insar_* with their per-epoch logs and final scores; held-out prediction maps and fitted offsets are under runs/insar_e1/oof, and the fringe-method outputs, including GeoTIFFs of the regime and mean flag frequency, under runs/insar_e1. The repository test suite passed 66 tests, including the fringe workflow on synthetic interferograms. Retention is on one machine; this report does not claim that an off-machine backup was created.
